item.title: Monday Storm Update: Lamont Lifts Commercial Vehicle Ban, Freezing Temps Expected All Week
item.description: Snow totals varied across the state, according to the National Weather Service, with totals so far ranging from just over a foot in the southern parts of the state to more than 18 inches in northern areas.

item.title: CT Severe Weather Protocol Extended Into February As Bitter Cold Expected To Last 10 More Days
item.description: The protocol was initially enacted on Friday, Jan. 23, 2026, and had been originally set to expire on Wednesday, Jan. 28. However, the updated forecast now indicates that bitterly cold weather will remain even longer, with well below normal temperatures persisting into the middle of next week.

item.title: CT Senate Eyes Legislation Clearing Path For Civil Rights Lawsuits Against Federal Agents Including ICE
item.description: State Sen. Matt Lesser and fellow Democratic state senators Martin Looney and Gary Winfield of New Haven and Bob Duff of Norwalk announced their intention to pass a state civil rights law in the upcoming legislative session

item.title: As Animal Cruelty Cases Rise In Connecticut, Advocates Push To Elevate Starvation To A Felony
item.description: Connecticut lawmakers and animal welfare advocates, including Desmond’s Army, a volunteer nonprofit of animal law advocates, unveiled a legislative package aimed at tightening the state’s response to animal abuse. Supporters say cruelty cases are rising while meaningful legal consequences are increasingly rare.

item.title: Blumenthal: Democrats To Vote To Deny DHS Funding Without Reform
item.description: The country is at a moral moment, with an out-of-control federal agency using police state tactics and killing American citizens in public, according to U.S. Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-CT.

item.title: CABE Sets Legislative Priorities For Upcoming Session
item.description: Patrice McCarthy, CABE’s executive director and general counsel, described education in Connecticut as “an army of individuals trying to provide the best possible education for our state.”

item.title: Former US Education Leader Cites Working Conditions, Teacher Pay As Top Issues Facing CT Educators
item.description: The Meriden native addressed the 2026 Connecticut Education Issues Summit Wednesday, tying his own background to the possibilities that open up when youths have access to a strong education system.

item.title: Do Teachers Have Free Speech? CT Panel Grapples With The Issue At Education Summit
item.description: State Sen. John Kissel, R-Enfield, said teachers shouldn’t have to choose between basic American freedoms and their career.
